2.7 Piano Keyboard (Buzzer)

Building an interactive one-octave piano keyboard using the passive buzzer with PWM tones.

Overview

This project creates a more sophisticated buzzer application: a visual piano keyboard where each key plays a specific musical note. It demonstrates complex widget layout, PWM frequency control, and multi-element UI design.

What You’ll Learn

  • Designing a custom multi-widget layout (7 white keys + 5 black keys)

  • Generating musical frequencies with PWM (ledcWriteTone())

  • Using a slider for volume control

  • Power switch to enable/disable audio output

How the Code Works

Keyboard Layout

The piano is laid out as an octave (C4 to B4):

// White keys
float notes[] = {261.63, 293.66, 329.63, 349.23, 392.00, 440.00, 493.88};
//               C4      D4      E4      F4      G4      A4      B4

static void key_cb(lv_event_t *e) {
    int note_idx = (int)lv_event_get_user_data(e);
    ledcWriteTone(0, notes[note_idx]);
}

Black Keys

Black keys are positioned overlapping the white keys (C#, D#, F#, G#, A#) — a classic piano layout achieved with LVGL’s absolute positioning.

Volume Slider

A slider adjusts the PWM duty cycle / amplitude to control volume:

static void volume_cb(lv_event_t *e) {
    int vol = lv_slider_get_value(slider);
    ledcWrite(0, vol);  // PWM duty for amplitude
}

Expected Result

  • A 12-key piano keyboard (7 white + 5 black) displayed on screen

  • Tapping any key plays the corresponding musical note

  • Volume slider adjusts loudness

  • Power switch enables/disables the keyboard

Touch and hold a key to sustain the note; release to stop.
